tasks.description:
Build single message and file removal on the Community server (apps/community) and the shared remove-in-place module that member erasure and the host takedown use. Depends on member erasure 1.1 (#2029, migration 0013: entry_redactions, community_content_versions, entries_author_key_unique, erasure.ts helpers). Migration: the next free number at build time (after 0013 erasure, 0014 hold, 0015 short names, 0016 import). MUST land before member erasure task 2.1 (the redaction feed, DOR-2266) is built.

### Tombstone texts (constants `REMOVED_ENTRY_TEXT` in new `src/content-removal.ts`)
- author (or their agent): `This message was deleted.` → removed_by 'author'
- owner or admin: `This message was removed by a community admin.` → 'moderator'
- host (takedown spec): `This message was removed by the host.` → 'host'
Kept on the row: author_display_name, author_member_id, author_agent_id, seq, parent_entry_id, thread_root_entry_id, created_at, idempotency_key. `payload_hash` becomes tombstonePayloadHash(text, parentEntryId) = SHA-256 of JSON {"text":<tombstone>,"mentions":[],"parentEntryId":<unchanged>,"attachmentIds":[]} (erasure's helper gains the text parameter). Erasure keeps `This message was erased.` / `Erased member` / `Erased agent`; erasure wins over removal; removing an already erased entry changes nothing.

### Migration
`entries.removed_at timestamptz NULL`, `entries.removed_by text NULL CHECK (removed_by IN ('author','moderator','host'))`, `CHECK ((removed_at IS NULL) = (removed_by IS NULL))`. Mirror in src/schema.ts, add to src/migrate.ts. Old code ignores the columns.

### Module `src/content-removal.ts`
```ts
/** Replace an entry's content with a tombstone and remove its mentions and files, in place. */
export async function removeEntry(client: PoolClient, input: { communityId: string; entryId: string; removedBy: 'author' | 'moderator' | 'host' }): Promise<{ changed: boolean; channelId: string; blobKeys: string[] }>;
/** Remove one file; tombstone its message when nothing is left in it. */
export async function removeAttachment(client: PoolClient, input: { communityId: string; attachmentId: string; removedBy: 'author' | 'moderator' | 'host' }): Promise<{ entryId: string | null; entryTombstoned: boolean; blobKeys: string[] }>;
```
removeEntry (caller already took communities FOR SHARE and checked lifecycle and actor):
1. SELECT the entry WHERE id AND community_id FOR NO KEY UPDATE (not FOR UPDATE: a reply holds FOR KEY SHARE on its parent while holding its channel). Missing → 404. removed_at or erased_at set → return changed:false.
2. bumpContentVersion (moved from erasure.ts): UPDATE community_content_versions SET version=version+1 — takes the row lock and holds it to commit. MUST run BEFORE any entry_redactions insert: identity values are assigned at insert, not commit, so inserting first lets two removals commit out of id order and a reader holding cursor N+1 would never see row N. Locking first serializes content changes per community so ids become visible in assignment order. The redaction feed (erasure task 2.1, DOR-2266) and the export rebuild depend on this; this task must land before that feed is built.
3. UPDATE entries SET text=tombstone, payload_hash=tombstone hash, removed_at=now(), removed_by.
4. DELETE FROM entry_mentions WHERE community_id AND entry_id.
5. DELETE FROM attachments WHERE community_id AND entry_id RETURNING blob_key; queueBlobs(client, communityId, keys) (moved from erasure.ts: managed_blobs state 'pending_delete' for committed/stored rows + pending_blob_deletions row, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
6. INSERT INTO entry_redactions(community_id, channel_id, entry_id).
removeAttachment:
1. SELECT the attachment WHERE id AND community_id FOR UPDATE, then re-read entry_id from the locked row (a post binding an unbound upload takes the same row lock, so the binding cannot change under the removal; no deadlock because a concurrently created entry is invisible until commit).
2. Bound: lock the entry FOR NO KEY UPDATE; bump the content version; delete the attachments row; queue its blob; if the entry's text is empty and no other file remains, run removeEntry steps 3, 4 and 6; else insert one entry_redactions row for the entry.
3. Unbound: delete the row, queue its blob; no bump, no redaction row.
Refactor (in this task): erasure.ts calls queueBlobs, bumpContentVersion, tombstonePayloadHash and the redaction insert from content-removal.ts and adopts bump-before-insert in every transaction that inserts redaction rows (today tombstone() and rewriteMentions() insert then bump). eraseFiles also inserts one entry_redactions row per BOUND entry whose file it deleted (instead of a bump with no row). Erasure suites must pass otherwise unchanged.

### Authority
New `requireRemovalPrincipal(c, auth, pool)` in data.ts: a browser session for a live member; a connection grant with 'post' in scopes and not history_only; or an agent credential. Host API key → 401. It applies this task's lifecycle rule (active, archived, held), not the posting rule. In owner-archived communities only history_only grants survive, so removal there needs a browser session; in held communities (hold-keeps-access) kept post grants may remove. Content is ranked by its human: an agent's content counts as its owner member's (owner's agent = owner content; active admin's agent = that admin's content). Rules (checked in the transaction):
- agent credential: entries it authored, files it uploaded;
- member role 'member': entries/files by them or by an agent they own;
- admin: the above plus anything whose human (author, or author agent's owner) is not the owner and not an ACTIVE admin (members and their agents, former admins and their agents, erased husks, imported historical members);
- owner: anything.
Refused: 403 FORBIDDEN "You can't remove this message." An id not in the path's community: 404 NOT_FOUND (same as unknown).
Lifecycles: allowed in active, archived, held; suspended → 503 COMMUNITY_SUSPENDED; deletion_pending → 423 COMMUNITY_DELETION_PENDING. Archived channel is no barrier. Community row FOR SHARE.

### Routes (under /api/v1/communities/:communityId/… and the single-community alias; register in app.ts)
- `DELETE /entries/:entryId` → 200 { entry } (tombstone). Repeat on removed or erased entry → 200 current entry, no writes, no audit.
- `DELETE /attachments/:attachmentId` → bound: 200 { entry } (without the file, or its tombstone if nothing left); unbound: 204; repeat → 404.
New strict schema in packages/shared/src/community-wire.ts: `CommunityWireEntryRemoveResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ entry: CommunityWireEntrySchema })` with TSDoc. No new error code.
Audit (same transaction): audit_events actor_kind='member', actor_member_id = the member or the agent's owner, action entry.delete | entry.remove | attachment.delete | attachment.remove by actor kind, subject_id the entry or file id, changed_fields {text,mentions,attachments} or {attachments}, no values.

### Replay of the original post
POST /channels/:id/entries: when the row found by (author, channel, idempotency_key) has removed_at or erased_at set, return its current projection with 200 (repeated) whatever the payload; never insert.

### Invariant (the real rule) and guard
1. Any change to what an EXISTING entry shows (text, mentions, files, author name) bumps the content version first, then writes one entry_redactions row for that entry, same transaction.
2. A bump without redaction rows is allowed only for changes no export data segment holds: deleting export archives (erasure deleteExports, takedown deleteReadyExports) and member/agent row changes (erasure husk); exports read those at the end.
3. An unexplained bump (version moved, no mappable redaction row) makes the export worker re-check every data segment's entry and file set and rewrite differing segments (export-any-size spec).
Guard test: scan apps/community/src (not __tests__) case-insensitively, across line breaks and extra whitespace, with or without quoted identifiers, schema prefix, or alias, for: UPDATE entries; UPDATE attachments … SET … entry_id; DELETE FROM attachments; DELETE FROM entry_mentions; INSERT INTO entry_mentions; UPDATE entry_mentions. Every match outside content-removal.ts needs a marker comment on the line before, `// content-change: <key>`, with the key present in apps/community/src/__tests__/content-change-allowlist.json with a non-empty reason. No whole-file exemption. Initial keys: post-binds-new-entry (routes/entries.ts post: UPDATE attachments SET entry_id, INSERT INTO entry_mentions — entry created in the same transaction), unposted-upload-sweep (routes/attachments.ts ~L163 DELETE FROM attachments … entry_id IS NULL — no entry), tenant-deletion (deletion-worker.ts), import-restore (import worker, when it exists), erasure-rewrite-mentions (erasure.ts rewriteMentions — bumps then writes rows), erasure-files (erasure.ts eraseFiles — bumps then writes rows).

### Docs
API.md (routes, who, texts, replay), OPERATIONS.md (storage freed at once, bytes leave at next sweep), docs/guides/communities.mdx (for people), changelog fragment.

### Acceptance criteria (real Postgres; filesystem and S3 BlobStores; tenancy harness; purpose comment each)
- AC-1 thread shape: M posts root R (mentions Q, one file); Q replies. M deletes R. R keeps id, seq, parent/thread ids, created_at, author id and name; history returns text `This message was deleted.`, mentions [], attachments []; parses with unchanged CommunityWireEntrySchema; Q's reply still names R; thread query on R returns the reply; page and stream resume cursors taken before still work (no 410).
- AC-2 nothing left: R text contains canary-text; file canary-file.txt with bytes canary-bytes. After delete + one blob sweep, a scan of every text/varchar/text[]/json/jsonb/bytea column from information_schema.columns (bytea searched as bytes and as UTF-8), every BlobStore object, and captured logs finds no canary, no SHA-256 of the file bytes, no SHA-256 of R's original payload. Control: the scan finds each before, including the file name inside export_segments.entries_index of an export made before (once export-any-size lands). Named leftover: that ready export holds R until it expires, by design; assert exactly that, expire it (clock), rescan clean. GET /attachments/<id> → 404.
- AC-3 storage at once: with a storage limit, host usage countedBytes drops by the file size in the same request; an upload that would have exceeded the limit before now succeeds.
- AC-4 authority matrix: member own 200, own agent 200, other member 403; agent own 200, sibling agent 403; admin: member's 200, member's agent's 200, owner's 403, owner's agent's 403, active admin's 403, active admin's agent's 403, former admin's 200, erased husk's 200; owner any 200; grant without post 403; history_only grant 403 (owner-archived community: browser session 200); held community with a kept post grant 200; host API key 401; community B's entry id under A's path 404. Refused requests change no row (counts and a digest of A's entries).
- AC-5 lifecycles: active, archived, held allowed; suspended 503; deletion_pending 423.
- AC-6 repeat/replay: deleting twice → same tombstone, one audit row, one entry_redactions row; retrying the original post with its key (same payload, and a different payload) → 200 tombstone, no new entry.
- AC-7 one file: text + two files → delete one leaves text and other file, one redaction row, deleted file 404; empty text + one file → deleting the file tombstones the message; unbound upload → uploader deletes 204, blob queued, no redaction row.
- AC-8 concurrency: a reply to R and a delete of R together (barrier) both succeed, no deadlock; delete racing erasure of M converges to the erased tombstone; an export snapshotted before the delete and committed after (hook) → 409, no blob left. Redaction order barrier: removal A bumps and pauses before inserting its redaction row; removal B blocks on the version row until A commits; B's id > A's and becomes visible after A's; a reader polling entry_redactions by id never sees B's row while A's lower id is missing (fails if bump comes after insert). Binding race: removing an unbound upload while a post binds it (barrier on the attachment row) ends with either the upload removed before the bind (post 409, file gone) or the file bound then removed with a redaction row; never a bound file queued for deletion without a redaction row.
- AC-9 audit: one audit_events row per removal with action, actor, subject, changed fields; no canary in its values.
- AC-10 member erasure suites (#2029) pass unchanged after the refactor.
- AC-11 guard: passes on the tree; fixture strings are each caught: `update ENTRIES set`, `UPDATE "entries" e SET`, `UPDATE public.entries`, a statement split across lines, `UPDATE attachments AS a SET entry_id`, `INSERT INTO entry_mentions`, `DELETE FROM\n  attachments`; a matched statement whose marker key is missing from the allowlist fails; an empty reason fails.
- Unit: tombstonePayloadHash(text,parent) fixed vector; the rank rule table.

tasks.description:
Add message and file deletion to the Community browser (apps/community/src/browser). Depends on task 1.1 (routes DELETE /entries/:entryId and DELETE /attachments/:attachmentId returning { entry } per CommunityWireEntryRemoveResponseSchema, 204 for an unbound upload).

### Behaviour
- Message menu: on your own message (or one by an agent you own) show **Delete**; on someone else's, for the owner, or for an admin when the author is not the owner and not an active admin, show **Remove**. Hide both on tombstones.
- Confirm dialogs (copy follows writing-for-humans, exact text):
  - Delete: "Delete this message? Everyone will see "This message was deleted." in its place. Its files are deleted too. This can't be undone." [Cancel] **Delete**
  - Remove: "Remove this message? Everyone will see "This message was removed by a community admin." in its place. Its files are deleted too. This can't be undone." [Cancel] **Remove**
  - Both add: "People who already saw it may have a copy, and exports made before now still contain it until they expire."
- File chip menu: **Delete file** / **Remove file** with "Delete this file? It's removed from the message and deleted. This can't be undone."
- After success, replace the entry in the local view with the returned entry (no reload).
- Tombstone rendering: an entry whose text equals one of `This message was deleted.`, `This message was removed by a community admin.`, `This message was removed by the host.`, or `This message was erased.` renders in muted italics, keeps its place and replies, and has no menu. Threads whose root is a tombstone still open.
- Errors: show the server's plain sentence.
- Works at phone, tablet, desktop widths.

### Acceptance criteria (apps/community/browser-tests, Playwright)
- Delete on own message shows the dialog text above and, after confirm, the tombstone in place with replies intact.
- Remove as an admin on a member's message works; the Remove item is absent on the owner's message for an admin.
- Delete file removes only that file chip; the message text stays.
- A tombstone has no menu.
- The dialog sentences match exactly (a copy test).

tasks.description:
Make removals reach open browser tabs and DorkOS mirrors through the redaction feed. Depends on task 1.1 and on member erasure task 2.1 (the redaction feed `GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/channels/:id/redactions?cursor=&limit=` returning current projections of entries with entry_redactions rows, signed cursor with redaction_epoch, 410 on a stale cursor; and the DorkOS mirror sync in apps/server/src/services/communities/remote/).

### Browser
While a channel is open, poll its redaction feed every 30 seconds and on window focus, from a cursor kept in memory (start from the feed's current end when the channel opens: the first page after load needs no replay because history was just loaded; on 410, restart from the end). Replace entries in place with each returned projection. Stop polling when the channel closes. No new stream event (strict parsers in DorkOS).

### DorkOS
No code change expected: the erasure 2.1 mirror sync is generic over redaction rows. Add a test proving it for a removal (not an erasure): the external author name is NOT changed for a removal (only erasure changes it).

### Acceptance criteria
- AC-12: after R is deleted, the redaction feed for R's channel returns R's tombstone projection (strict-schema valid). A DorkOS test server mirroring the channel (erasure 2.1 harness) replaces the cached text with the tombstone after one feed sync, keeps the author's display name, dispatches no local agent, and message search no longer finds R's original text. A second browser tab showing R shows the tombstone within one poll (Playwright, fake timers or a 30 s wait).
